Installation, dependencies and software versions

installation.Rmd

Software versions

These tables record the environment used to validate the tutorials. Keep vegan at 2.7.2; the other version numbers document the tested environment.

Table 1. Software used for tutorial validation
Software Version Role
MicroFun 0.1.0 Package documented on this website
R 4.5.3 Patched (r90083) Analysis runtime
Bioconductor 3.22 Bioconductor release in the validation environment
RStudio (optional) 2024.09.1+394 Installed IDE and bundled Pandoc
vegan 2.7.2 (CRAN spelling 2.7-2) Required exact version

The only dependency with an exact-version requirement is vegan. This pin matters for the stratified workflow, where some genera have zero contributions in individual samples. Use a fresh R session after installing it. The CRAN archive distributes the required release as vegan_2.7-2.tar.gz; R treats 2.7.2 and 2.7-2 as the same package version. Record the exact versions resolved in your own analysis session with sessionInfo().

Why install from a source folder?

The source folder contains the functions, reference tables and documentation that belong together. Installing that folder helps ensure you are using one consistent copy. The folder itself should contain DESCRIPTION; pointing R at its parent folder is a common cause of installation errors.

Install the source package

Download the source ZIP from the MicroFun repository. Extract it into a folder containing DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE and R/. Replace path/to/MicroFun below with that folder. Restart R before replacing a loaded package.

source_dir <- "path/to/MicroFun"
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(source_dir, "DESCRIPTION")))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")

imports <- read.dcf(file.path(source_dir, "DESCRIPTION"), fields = "Imports")[1, 1]
dependencies <- trimws(strsplit(imports, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
dependencies <- sub("[[:space:]]*\\(.*$", "", dependencies)
dependencies <- unique(c(dependencies, "KEGGREST", "R.utils", "rsvg", "qpdf", "svglite"))
BiocManager::install(setdiff(dependencies, "vegan"), ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
install.packages(source_dir, repos = NULL, type = "source")

# Install the required vegan release.
remotes::install_version("vegan", version = "2.7-2",
                         repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", upgrade = "never")
stopifnot(packageVersion("vegan") == package_version("2.7.2"))
library(MicroFun)

If vegan was already loaded, restart R after changing its version before running an analysis. Installing this archived release from source requires a working compiler toolchain. On macOS, use the matching Fortran compiler from the R for macOS tools page; on Windows, use the Rtools version for your R release.

If dependency installation fails

If installation reports missing or unavailable Bioconductor dependencies, install the following packages with BiocManager, then retry installing MicroFun. See the Bioconductor installation guide for repository and installation help.

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(
  c("ALDEx2", "DESeq2", "edgeR", "lefser", "limma", "Maaslin2", "metagenomeSeq"),
  update = FALSE, ask = FALSE
)
install.packages(source_dir, repos = NULL, type = "source")

rsvg enables tree Sankey PNG/PDF export; qpdf enables continuation-page PDF export. svglite is used by ggsave() for the Standard SVG figures. Chord SVG/HTML uses R’s Cairo SVG device. On macOS, if export reports a missing /opt/X11 library or a failed Cairo DLL, install XQuartz and restart R before exporting.

Local KO–KEGG mapping and online annotation

Mapping and annotation answer different questions. The KO-to-KEGG pathway mapping defines which KOs belong to each pathway and is used to sum their predicted abundances. Annotation adds readable names and categories to the resulting identifiers.

Table 4. Local reference data and KEGG network access
Step Data source and behaviour KEGG connection required
KO-to-KEGG pathway abundance conversion ko2kegg_abundance() uses the bundled ko_to_kegg_reference by default, or a local mapping supplied through kegg_map. No
Local KO descriptions Standard reads KO and KoDescription from the bundled KO_reference.RData dictionary and matches the KO IDs. No
Local EC or MetaCyc descriptions pathway_annotation(..., ko_to_kegg = FALSE) uses the corresponding bundled reference files. No
Online KEGG pathway annotation pathway_annotation(..., ko_to_kegg = TRUE) uses KEGGREST to query KEGG for names and classification information. Entries already queried may be reused from the current R session’s cache. Yes
Plotting fitted study results PCA, heatmap and error-bar calls reuse the matrices and annotation tables created in Standard. No additional connection after annotation

The bundled KO–KEGG mapping is a local snapshot, not a live connection to KEGG. It does not update automatically when online annotations are retrieved. The supplied mapping does not include a clearly identified KEGG release or retrieval date, so it should not be described as the latest KEGG mapping. If you supply your own mapping, retain that file and record its source, release or retrieval date alongside the results. Keep the same mapping for abundance aggregation, analysis and plotting.

Academic users accessing the standard KEGG REST service do not need to apply for an API key or enter one in MicroFun. MicroFun makes the annotation requests through KEGGREST; you need the package installed and a working connection to KEGG. See the KEGG API access conditions and REST interface documentation.

The taxon-centered stratified KO workflow performs local KO-to-pathway aggregation, then requests online KEGG annotation as part of pathway_sdaa(). Supplying a local kegg_map changes the membership mapping; it does not disable that annotation request. Taxon-centered input already containing KEGG pathway IDs also uses online pathway annotation. The function-centered KO workflow keeps the KO identifiers and does not invoke this KEGG pathway annotation step.

Once the software is installed, local-reference steps and plotting saved annotated results can run without contacting KEGG. Initial software installation may still require internet access. An annotation connection failure is a reason to check network access or KEGG availability, rather than look for a missing API key.

Before you move on

Load MicroFun in a fresh R session and check that the installation completed without missing-package messages. If a plotting or export function asks for an optional dependency, install the package used by that feature rather than changing your analysis inputs. The troubleshooting guide separates input issues from plotting and export issues.

Record the resolved environment 

sessionInfo()
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "MicroFun_sessionInfo.txt")

Continue with Study data and downloads, or prepare your own study.

The current source also supports MaAsLin2 transformations, mean-contribution top_n boxplot selection, and scientific-notation error-bar p-value labels. See analysis options. Function-centered descriptive labels in the demonstration are explicitly supplied for presentation, not new analysis identifiers.
